title: Joining Billy Shaw's agency; Bill Davis at Birdland; Joe Glaser
summary: Shaw persuades him to become an agent; he gets Bill Davis into Birdland and recalls Joe Glaser wanting big records.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yeah, right. So Billy Shaw called me over. He'd lost a guy, and he wanted to hire me as an agent. And I wasn't too cool about being an agent, but I was really disgusted with my operation going on, because they just wasn't takin' care of business back here like I wanted it to be taken care of. Because we had a thing going. So he talked me... He talked a hole in my head. He said, "As long as you're a personal manager, you ain't nothin' but a flunky. You got to go and hang up the clothes. If they want something to eat, you got to go out and get a sandwich." He said, "When you're a booking agent... My philosophy, if I lose one, I gain two." He had just started doing good, because he had got ahold of a couple of good artists who was doing one-nighters for him." So it sounded so good, so I said, "Well..." This was right after Thanksgiving. So I said, "Let's make a deal. I'll start to work for you the first of the year." So that's when I made a deal to go to work for Billy Shaw. So after I got over there, I started booking the attractions I had. And I still had my management on Bill Davis and Bill Doggett. So then he wanted a contract on Bill Davis. So I told the guy that was booking the clubs, I said, "If you get Bill Davis in Birdland, I'll sign him a contract." So he did. And Birdland thought he was the
organ player that made the record with Ella Fitzgerald, but it was Bill Doggett that had made the record with Ella Fitzgerald... But anyway, he got into Birdland.

And I had tried to check with Joe Glaser (I knew him then) for him to book Bill Davis. Because I knew what he could do, but they didn't know what he could do. And he didn't have a big enough record... Because Joe Glaser was funny. Unless you had a big record, he didn't want to be bothered with you. I understood it. And he booked Bill Davis... I forget who he booked him in there with. But he broke up Birdland. Because he had Chris Columbo and Bill Jennings, just a trio.
